findings.old_str: How does Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) enable database engines to guarantee ACID

findings.summary: Add the three discovery links reported by R3 without changing wording.
Remove the generated paragraph width rule; R5 also reports table width/min-width rules.
findings.fix_blocker: The rules are absent from the durable spec and direct generated-page edits are prohibited; resolve the durable generator/source first.

findings.old_str: wrapping these operations in an ACID transaction guarantees that the customer cannot be charged if the inventory deduction fails.
findings.new_str: a database transaction can atomically couple the inventory and order-row changes, but it cannot atomically include an external card charge without an additional distributed workflow such as authorization, idempotency, compensation, and reconciliation.
findings.summary: Do not claim a database transaction covers an external payment system.

findings.old_str: read-write transactions operate exclusively under serializable isolation with external consistency, preventing all concurrency anomalies globally without requiring manual lock management from application developers.
findings.new_str: serializable isolation is Spanner's default and provides external consistency; Spanner also documents repeatable-read read-write transactions, so architects must state the selected isolation and its guarantees rather than claim exclusivity or the absence of every application-level anomaly.

findings.rule: Product claims require supporting opened sections
findings.old_str: High-throughput financial or retail systems requiring analytical acceleration and sub-second failover leverage AlloyDB;
findings.new_str: Workloads considering AlloyDB must validate transactional throughput, analytical acceleration, failover behavior, recovery objectives and cost against current documentation and a workload-specific test;
findings.summary: Remove the unsupported sub-second failover selection rule.

findings.rule: Product benchmarks require scoped primary-source support
findings.old_str: up to 4x faster transactional throughput than standard PostgreSQL.
findings.new_str: performance characteristics that must be evaluated against current AlloyDB documentation and the learner's workload; this lesson does not establish a comparative throughput multiplier.
findings.summary: Remove an unscoped vendor benchmark unsupported by the cited Day 16 sources.

findings.rule: State only what the cited product section supports
findings.old_str: continuous WAL archiving streams WAL segments to a dedicated Google Cloud Storage bucket.
findings.new_str: Cloud SQL uses transaction logs for point-in-time recovery when PITR is enabled; current documentation describes configurable log retention and Cloud Storage transaction-log storage without exposing a learner-managed dedicated bucket.
findings.summary: Bound the Cloud SQL PITR storage statement to documented behavior.

findings.old_str: preserving the inventory invariant with 100% mathematical certainty.
findings.new_str: preserving the database stock lower-bound invariant for this transaction when the statement succeeds and its affected-row result is handled correctly.
findings.summary: Replace the absolute guarantee with its actual transactional boundary.

findings.rule: Do not call predicted staging evidence verified
findings.old_str: item constraint failure; verified that 100% of staged changes were rolled back, leaving zero orphaned
findings.new_str: item constraint failure; would check that the controlled staging run leaves zero orphaned
findings.summary: Keep expected scenario verification distinct from observed local lab evidence.

outside_roadmap_scope: Cloud Data Fusion, BigQuery federation, detailed Spanner internals, Cloud SQL Auth Proxy networking, and database product benchmarking exceed Day 16 unless retained only as brief, correctly sourced applicability notes.
Locking and deadlock practice remains assigned to Day 61; Day 16 should stop at ACID, a worked isolation anomaly, and commit/rollback.
